items: **Generics** let one class or method serve many types while keeping full compile-time type safety.
A **type parameter** (`T`, `E`, `K`, `V`, `N`) is a placeholder filled in when an object is created.
The **diamond** `<>` goes on the **right**; the declared type on the left is required.
Type arguments must be **reference types**: `Integer`, not `int`; autoboxing hides the conversion.
**`<?>`** is unbounded, **`<? extends T>`** upper bounded, **`<? super T>`** lower bounded.
Generic types are **invariant**: `List<String>` is not a `List<Object>`.
